ED Code Assist

Quick start & tips (tap to expand)
Diagnosis
  • Type any diagnosis — patient language works too (heart attack, sob, twisted ankle). Ranked, billable FY2026 codes only.
  • Amber ⚠ chips mark symptom / unspecified codes — still selectable, never blocked. Tap a row for more specific alternatives and coding notes.
  • ★ marks a code on the department's ED preferred diagnosis list (clinical governance v2.0).
Presenting complaint
  • One or more complaints, comma-separated — one card each: column 1 the symptom code, column 2 the differentials (red = not-to-miss).
Clinical notes
  • Paste the note, then press any of the three buttons — every one runs the DDx step first (when the note has no DDx items yet), then does its own analysis: the ICD-10 codes from the DDx + the note, a DDx-targeted workup, or the note audit. Purple buttons send the note to the AI endpoint; the Audit button runs the offline checks locally and an AI auditor pass — what is shown is what the AI auditor flags (by both auditors, or by the AI auditor alone); items flagged only by the offline auditor are skipped. The items the auditors agree are documented sit minimized in one ✓ N documented line — click it to expand their evidence; the wrong and the controversial items stay expanded. The left panel (and keys 1-6) jumps between the notes subsections; the Clinical Note entry shows the audit score after an AI audit (never on the offline view), and the audit section folds with its own Expand / Collapse pair at its top and bottom.
  • One ICD-10 dashboard holds both code lists, in two subsections: DDx-based ICD (the suggested DDx, working diagnosis first, each differential with its code — + Notes appends a differential to the note (extending an existing DDx line with “, + dx”), + adds its code to the tray — from the diagnosis row or the code row — and the two Add all buttons sit at the top) and Clinical-Based ICD (the codes suggested from the clinical note itself — hover a code for its coding rationale). Every code keeps its buttons on its own row; the Expand / Collapse pairs at the top and bottom fold the whole dashboard; the workup runs only after the DDx items exist.
  • The Suggested workup is cross-checked against the ED CPG (clinical governance): investigations on the CPG carry a ★ CG badge, and the CPG items the other guidelines (ACEP / Tintinalli's / Rosen's / Harwood-Nuss') missed are added and marked the same way. Every card is orderable — clicking a card orders the investigation, and the reason in the labs-reasoning box below is written by the AI for this encounter (from the DDx + the notes, in “X is done to exclude …” style with varied wording), with Copy and Add to clinical notes buttons. CPG items the current notes do not justify are compared against the other guidelines in use and carry a ⚠ needs supporting data note — “add supporting data like …” — with the standing rule: only if genuinely asked, examined, or found.
  • Every AI code is validated against the official FY2026 list — no invented codes. ★ = on the ED preferred list.
  • Ordered something outside the suggested workup? List it in the Justify box (the DDx step runs first): a candid advisory verdict (never copied) plus a ready-to-paste clinical-note draft with evidence links — and when the investigation is not justified by the available data, a gap box appears: the explanation is advisory and can never be copied or added to the notes, while each isolated indication that would have justified it gets its own Copy and Add-to-notes button — with the standing reminder to never fake a complaint, an examination finding, or a result.
  • Long how-it-works prose sits behind the small ⓘ icons — click one to read the logic behind any section.
Selected codes
  • The tray collects this encounter's codes — reorder for the coding sequence (the first code is the principal diagnosis), copy in EMR formats, or export CSV.
  • Every removal offers Undo; the tray survives a page reload. Delete codes clears the tray (undo offered); New Patient in the top panel resets the whole encounter — note, results, the justify box and the tray.
  • Keyboard: / focuses search, ↑↓ navigate, Enter adds the highlighted code. Full list in Keyboard shortcuts below.
Keyboard shortcuts
Alt+Q suggest codes (notes, DDX, ICD) Alt+A suggested workup Alt+Y justify with AI Assist Alt+N new patient Alt+J justify box Alt+C copy suggested codes 1-6 jump between the notes subsections (the left panel)

• The Diagnosis and Complaint tabs run 100% offline in this single file — that data never leaves this machine. The Notes tab's AI features send the note text to the admin-configured external endpoint per your governance policy; every displayed code is still validated against the official CMS ICD-10-CM FY2026 release (no invented codes). This is a decision-support aid, not a substitute for clinical coding judgment.

Notes sections
ⓘ how it works
Workflow: 1 paste the note · 2 press notes, DDX, ICD — it runs the DDx step first, then suggests the codes; Suggested workup (Alt+A) then builds on those DDx items — it stays disabled until they exist and never re-runs the DDx step; only Audit notes audits the notes alone, no DDx call · 3 click workup cards to order them — their reasons draft below · 4 justify tests ordered outside the suggested workup — the tray on the right collects your final codes.
Purple buttons use the configured endpoint · offline checks stay local
ⓘ how it works
Purple buttons send the note to the admin-configured endpoint (internet required; Groq by default) — the offline audit checks run locally; the only Audit notes button also runs an AI auditor pass on the endpoint. The DDx step runs first for notes, DDX, ICD and the justification; Suggested workup reuses the DDx items already generated (no extra DDx call), and only Audit notes never needs the DDx.
ICD-10 dashboard
Justify workup outside the suggested list
ⓘ how it works
Ordered labs or imaging that are not in the suggested workup above? List them here — the DDx step runs first, then AI Assist replies: a candid verdict (advisory — cannot be copied; it keeps the textbook tone and the references, ACEP / Tintinalli's / Rosen's / Harwood-Nuss'), a justification draft written in clinical-note phrasing (short documentation sentences like “CRP done to exclude systemic infection or inflammation”, ready to paste straight into the notes), and evidence links to check each citation. When the investigation is not justified by the available data (the DDx + the clinical notes), a gap box appears, split in two: the explanation of what is missing is advisory — not copyable, never added to the notes — while the isolated indications that would have justified it sit underneath, each with its own Copy and Add to notes button so every indication is handled on its own, after verifying it was genuinely asked, examined, or found. The reminder stands: never fake a complaint, an examination finding, or a result.

Data & build info
Data: official CMS ICD-10-CM FY2026 (April 2026 release) · 37941 ED-relevant billable codes (filtered from 74,719; every suggestion validated against the full official list of 98186 codes) · 90 ED presenting complaints · ED preferred diagnosis list v2.0 (clinical governance, 449 codes) · ED CPG investigations (clinical governance, placeholder v1.0-seed pending the CG's CPG file) · update 2.8 · built 2026-10-18 · the ⚙ Admin settings, the theme picker and the Quick start & tips guide all live in the top panel row
What's new
  • 2.8 — token saving, a focused keyboard map, and Tintinalli’s indexed: Suggested workup now stays disabled until notes, DDX, ICD has generated the DDx items for the note — it then builds on those DDx items + the clinical notes with no extra DDx call; only Audit notes (renamed) audits the notes alone — the offline checks + AI auditor exactly as before, no DDx refresh — and clicking it jumps to the audit section. The keyboard map is now Alt+Q codes · Alt+A workup · Alt+Y AI justify · Alt+N new patient (each shown on the button hover; Ctrl+Enter and Alt+W retired). Tintinalli’s joined Harwood-Nuss’ as an indexed reference: the workup and justification prompts carry a verified chapter index of the 9th edition (304 chapters, from the book’s official chapter list) and cite it chapter-by-chapter — every Tintinalli chapter citation links to the official chapter-list page, so a chapter number is never invented. The default AI model is now gpt-oss-120b (strong reasoning) instead of llama-3.3-70b-versatile · fresh devices and Reset to built-in defaults pick it up; a device with saved Admin settings keeps its saved model.
  • 2.7 — the guideline references now run on ACEP (the American College of Emergency Physicians) instead of NICE: the workup and justification prompts cite ACEP clinical policies by topic — never an invented policy ID — and every ACEP citation carries a link to ACEP’s verified clinical-policies page so each citation can be checked. Tintinalli’s, Rosen’s, Harwood-Nuss’ and the department CPG are unchanged.
  • 2.6 — the + now reaches every differential in DDx-based ICD: the DDx step returns a suggested ICD code for each differential in every case — including when the note documents the working diagnosis (until now those differentials carried no code, so no + appeared at all). A differential whose code fails validation (or that the AI leaves without one) simply shows no + — it can never pick up a neighbouring differential's code. The + Notes buttons are untouched.
  • 2.5 — in DDx-based ICD, every differential with a suggested code now carries its own + on the diagnosis row — one click adds that differential's code to the selected codes (the code row keeps its +). In Clinical-Based ICD, the coding rationale moved onto the code hover — hover a code to read why it was suggested; the listing stays lean. The codes button is now notes, DDX, ICD. The Clinical notes audit section gained the same Expand / Collapse pair at its top and bottom.
  • 2.4 — the ICD-10 dashboard folds: an Expand / Collapse pair beside the title and the same pair again at the end of the section, so it collapses without scrolling back up (either pair works; jumping to a subsection re-expands it). Adding differentials one by one now reads like a doctor writes: when the note already carries a DDx line, + Notes extends it with “, + differential” instead of opening another line. The codes button was renamed (see 2.5 — notes, DDX, ICD). The clinical-notes left panel entry Audit became Clinical Note — the shortcuts stay, and after an AI audit the entry shows the score (e.g. 6/9); the offline audit shows no score.
  • 2.3 — the DDx and the ICD sections merged into one ICD-10 dashboard: the first subsection is DDx-based ICD (the suggested DDx and their codes — the copy buttons were deleted; + Notes and + stay, and Add all DDx to clinical notes / Add all DDx codes moved to the top), the second is Clinical-Based ICD (the codes suggested from the clinical note itself). Every ICD code now keeps its buttons on its own row. The live note-audit pill was deleted — a better indicator will come later. The AI auditor now counts the ER course as documented when investigations are documented in general wording (labs / bloods / Ix / rads / imaging, even without results), ED medications are given, or a consultation is documented.
  • 2.2 — the audit list is decluttered: the items the auditors agree are documented collapse into one ✓ N documented line (click to expand and re-check their evidence), while the wrong and the controversial items (the auditors disagree) stay expanded. Every section's how-it-works prose now sits behind a small ⓘ icon — the workflow line, the button-bar note, the DDx / codes / workup / ordered-reasons / justification footers and the audit rules, all collapsed by default, one click to read. New Patient (and Clear note & results) now also clears the Justify workup box — the ordered-tests list dies with its encounter.
  • 2.1 — the note audit became a dual-auditor view: the offline checks and an AI auditor pass both run from the one Audit clinical notes button, and every item carries both verdicts (offline in teal, AI in purple). What is shown now follows the AI auditor: items flagged by both auditors — or by the AI auditor alone — are displayed; items flagged only by the offline auditor are skipped (it proved the less reliable of the two). The local audit runs instantly as before (Alt+A / the live pill), and the AI pass needs the endpoint — when it is unavailable the offline view stays with a notice. The sick-leave check now recognizes the duration wording (“Sick leave : 48 hrs” shows “duration: 48 hrs”; no duration shows “no duration stated”). The top panel is one row: the code-helper subtitle was deleted, and New Patient (clears the note, every result and the tray, undo for the codes) joined the tabs. The clinical-notes tab gained a left panel for moving between its subsections (icons + keys 1-6); Keyboard shortcuts moved into Quick start & tips; the tray’s clear button is now Delete codes; the long Data & build statement collapsed behind an expandable button; the justify how-it-works prose and the audit footnote stowed behind ⓘ toggles.
  • 1.6 — the suggested workup grew an honest layer for the CPG: every CPG-recommended investigation the current clinical notes do not justify is now compared against the other guidelines in use (NICE / Tintinalli's / Rosen's / Harwood-Nuss') and its card carries a ⚠ needs supporting data note — “add supporting data like …” with the specific findings that would justify the test — plus the standing rule that supporting data is added only if it was genuinely asked, examined, or found. The reason drafted when a card is ordered is now written by the AI for this encounter (from the DDx + the notes, in the established “X is done to exclude …” documentation style with varied wording) instead of assembled from fixed local phrase pools. The Quick start & tips guide and the ⚙ Admin settings both moved into the top panel — the guide is a strip in the header that drops down over the page, the admin button sits beside the tabs.
  • 1.5 — the gap box (investigation not justified by the available data) is now split in two: the explanation (“X was ordered, but no documented indication is present…”) is advisory only — not selectable, no buttons — so that first phase can never be copied or pasted into the clinical notes; the isolated indications that would have justified the investigation render underneath, each with its own Copy and Add to notes button, so every indication is handled solitarily (the anti-faking reminder stays). New colour theme setting in the header: Day, Sepia, Dark and Night — saved on this machine, restored before first paint.
  • 1.4 — the DDx step now runs FIRST as its own call: the ICD codes, the suggested workup and the justification of investigations all build on the suggested DDx (their user messages carry it, and none of them runs before it). The justification grew a gap box: when the investigation is not justified by the available data, it answers what could be missed or forgotten in the DDx or the clinical notes that would justify it — with the standing reminder to never fake a complaint, an examination finding, or a result. The Clinical Notes tab is now the default tab; the note audit accepts non-verbatim disposition plans ("the patient is for OPD", "for admission", "transferred to ward"); the Audit all button was removed — every button runs the DDx step itself, so the chain is no longer needed. The suggested workup is now cross-checked against the ED CPG (clinical governance): CPG investigations carry a ★ CG badge, the CPG items the other guidelines missed are added as cards, and every card is orderable — a click orders the investigation and drafts its reason in the labs-reasoning box (Copy / Add to clinical notes), with deliberately varied wording so the drafted reasons never read robotic. A LOGIC.md diagram of the whole page now ships alongside.
  • 1.3 — the Suggested DDx became a first-class panel that every Notes-tab button keeps fresh: each differential copies or adds to the clinical notes on its own (or all at once), differentials with suggested ICD codes carry them inline (+ adds to the tray); the suggested workup is now DDx-targeted — it runs only after the DDx items exist and orders tests that evaluate, confirm or risk-stratify them.
  • 1.2 — results quick-nav with counts; live note audit pill that updates as you type; audit shows what matched (found: “…”) and can insert the missing headings; encounter tray: reorder for coding sequence, 1st principal marker, Undo for every removal, New patient, EMR copy formats, survives a page reload; Cancel for AI calls; Esc closes dialogs and blurs before clearing; ★ shown only for preferred-list codes; accessibility and contrast fixes.
  • 1.1 — one-click Audit all; fuzzy abbreviations (C/O, PMHx, “opd fu”) and spelling slips never penalized; sick leave required unless DAMA / admission / death; justification drafts in clinical-note phrasing.
  • 1.0 — local note audit; DDx ready-to-copy with suggested DDx codes.
  • 0.9 — ED preferred-list stars; DDx line; evidence links for citations.

Diagnosis & Complaint tabs stay fully offline. The Notes tab uses AI Assist: note text goes to the admin-configured endpoint (Groq by default). Suggested workup reflects ACEP / Tintinalli's / Rosen's / Harwood-Nuss' practice and is decision support only — the physician remains responsible.

Clear selected codes first?

The selected-codes tray holds 0 code(s). AI Assist suggests codes from the pasted note — keep the tray if you are still building this encounter's list, or clear it to start fresh.

Admin settings — AI backend

For the ED administrator only. Regular users never need this screen; the built-in defaults (Groq, free tier) work out of the box.
Stored on this device only (browser localStorage), never in the distributed file unless you rebuild it. Users of this tool never see the key.
Privacy: AI Assist sends the pasted note text to this endpoint (an external service). Configure per your hospital's PHI policy before enabling physicians to use it.
